GENERAL PASSENGER INFORMATION
BAGGAGE - Baggage includes all luggage, parcels, and packages carried in the cabin or
checked in the cargo space.
Overcoats, umbrellas, ladies' handbags or ladies'
and small cameras carried by the passenger will not be weighed as
pocketbooks,

TWA may
limit the weight, size and type of baggage.
BAGGAGE ALLOWANCE-IN THE U.S.A.—On each ticket, except when travel is part of an
international trip by air, free baggage allowance is 2 checked bags,
1 with
dimensions
(length plus width plus height) not over 62 inches and 1 with dimensions not over 55 inches,
plus 1 or more pieces of underseat baggage with combined dimensions not over 45 inches.
INTERNATIONAL FIRST CLASS -66 Ibs. (30 kilograms) carried free for each full or half
fare first class ticket, including portions of travel in the U.S.A.
INTERNATIONAL ECONOMY CLASS-44 Ibs. (20 kilograms) carried free for
half fare economy class ticket, including portions of travel in the U.S.A.
CHILDREN - Children paying half fare are granted free baggage allowance on the same
basis as a passenger paying the full adult fare. Children traveling free or at the 10% fare
receive no free baggage allowance.
BAGGAGE-EXCESS CHARGES-Checked baggage in excess of the above free allowances shall
examine
baggage
on
arrival.
IN THE U.S.A.-When the adult jet coach fare between the points between which the bag-
gage is checked or from the passenger's origin to his destination is $25 or less, $2 per piece;
$25.01-50.00, $3 per piece; $50.01-120.00, $4 per piece; $120.01-200.00, $5 per piece;
over $200, $6 per piece.
INTERNATIONAL-Excess baggage is charged for at 1% of the full first class adult one way
jet fare per kilogram (2.2 Ibs.).
BAGGAGE-EXCESS VALUE-TWA's liability for baggage is limited to its actual value, but not
more than $500.00 per passenger on trips in the U.S.A. or $16.50 per kilogram for checked
baggage and $330 per passenger for unchecked baggage on international trips,
higher valuation is stated before the flight and a charge of 10g on trips in the U.S.A. or 15¢
on international trips is paid for each extra $100 or fraction thereof claimed.
CHECK-IN FOR FLIGHTS-INTERNATIONAL-The times shown for international flight check-in
are the minimum required for completion of government formalities. Flights cannot be de-
tained for passengers arriving late, and no responsibility can be accepted in such cases.
IN THE U.S.A.-TWA may cancel the reservation of any passenger who fails to present himself
for check-in at the ticket lifting point 5 minutes before scheduled departure time of domestic
U.S.A. flights.
CHILDREN-IN THE U.S.A.-(Not applicable to Family Fare travel)-(a) One child under 2
years not occupying a seat carried free with each accompanying fare paying adult passenger.
(b) Children under 2 years occupying a seat, or over 2 years and under 12 years, or more than
one child accompanying a passenger are each charged one half adult fare. (c) Children under
5 years must be accompanied by a passenger at least 12 years old. Children between 5 and 8
may travel alone only by prior arrangement. Unaccompanied children between the ages of 5
and 12 will be charged the full adult fare. INTERNATIONAL-One child under 2 years not occu-
pying a seat carried at 10% of adult fare with each accompanying full fare adult passenger.
Children over 2 and under 12 years, a child under 2 occupying a seat, and more than one child
accompanying a passenger are each charged one half adult fare. Children may travel alone
only under certain conditions.

Fruits, plants, meats and similar agricultural items can-
not be taken into the U.S.A. without permission. Consult the U.S. Department of Agriculture
or the nearest U.S. Foreign Office overseas for details. While TWA usually has available the
latest information, the carrier is not responsible for its accuracy and suggests that passen-
gers consult the nearest Consulate of the country to be visited.
FAMILY STYLE FARES-IN THE U.S.A.-When travel is via First Class or Coach service Mon-
day Noon through Friday Noon, or Friday Midnight through Sunday Noon, your spouse, or if
no accompanying spouse the first accompanying child 2 through 21 years,
of 25%. Additional accompanying children 2 through 11 receive a 663% discount; accom-
panying children 12 through 21 receive a 50% discount. Family discounts do not apply to
economy, jet commuter, or night coach fares. One infant under 2 years not occupying a seat
is carried free with each family group.
GROUND TRANSPORTATION - Taxicab and limousine service available between downtown
scheduled pick-up points and airport, at passenger's expense.
HOTEL RESERVATIONS-Any TWA office will gladly arrange hotel reservations in addition
to airline reservations.
INSURANCE Trip insurance is available at most airlines offices in the U.S.A.
MEAL SERVICE - For information on Food and Beverage Service, see schedule pages.
RECONFIRMATION - INTERNATIONAL - Passengers holding continuing or return reservations
must reconfirm their reservations at least 72 hours before scheduled flight departure time.
Failure to reconfirm will result in cancellation of all reservations.
RESERVATIONS - Reservations are not definite until tickets are purchased. Passage may
be retused to any person when necessary to comply with Government regulations, tariff
rules, or for reasons beyond the control of TWA.
SCHEDULES - TWA reserves the right to cancel or change schedules without notice. Safety
is our primary consideration. Schedules shown are based on expected flying times. Because
weather and other factors may affect operating conditions, departures and arrivals cannot
be guaranteed.
STOPOVERS-IN THE U.S.A.—Stopovers are not permitted on domestic U.S.A. tickets with-
out additional charge, except in connection with international air travel. INTERNATIONAL -
Within the time limit of the ticket, stopover will be permitted at any scheduled stop pro-
vided reservation is made and, on international flights, provided the passenger has a valid
visa if required by law.
HALF/FARE TRAVEL PLAN - IN THE U.S.A. - Reduced fares are avalaible for persons 12
through 21 years of age on a no-reservations basis at 50% of normal jet coach fares.
